status_summary: Executive Order 14159 (signed 2025-01-20), section 19, paused and ordered review of federal funding agreements with nongovernmental organizations that support removable aliens, and in February 2025 FEMA stopped funding under the Shelter and Services Program, which reimburses non-federal entities for sheltering noncitizens released from DHS custody, and clawed back more than 80 million dollars from New York City; a Manhattan judge declined on 2025-03-05 to order that money returned immediately. Bills to end the program and rescind its balances (S. 771 and H.R. 1668) were introduced on 2025-02-27; no enactment was found. On 2026-05-26 the Western District of Washington set aside the termination as applied to Washington and required FEMA to consider its reimbursement requests, without ordering payment. The redirect of the money to border and detention uses was not traced.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14159 was signed; section 19 directs the Attorney General and the Secretary of Homeland Security to review and audit funding agreements with nongovernmental organizations that support removable or illegal aliens, pause further distributions pending review, terminate agreements found unlawful or wasteful, and seek recoupment where appropriate.

S. 771 and H.R. 1668, the End FEMA Benefits for Illegal Immigrants Act, were introduced to bar FEMA from running a program that funds sheltering by non-federal entities to relieve CBP holding facilities and to rescind unobligated transferred balances.
A federal judge in Manhattan declined New York City's request for a temporary restraining order returning more than 80 million dollars in shelter funding that FEMA had clawed back in February 2025.
The State of Washington sued DHS and FEMA in the Western District of Washington (No. 2:25-cv-01401) over the end of its Shelter and Services Program award of about 4 million dollars.

The district court granted Washington summary judgment in part on its Administrative Procedure Act claims, set aside the program termination policy and the termination of Washington's award as applied to Washington, and barred FEMA from refusing to consider its reimbursement requests on the grounds held unlawful, without ordering payment.
